Portugal is a country on the Atlantic edge of the Iberian Peninsula. It became a kingdom under Afonso Henriques, who called himself king after a victory over the Moors in 1139, and its borders have changed little since the 1200s, among the oldest in Europe.

It was born in the Reconquista, the Christian advance against al-Andalus. Afonso took Lisbon in 1147 with the help of crusaders on their way east, and the south coast, the Algarve, was won by 1249. In 1385 a victory at Aljubarrota kept Portugal independent of Castile and put the house of Aviz on the throne.

Small and poor, Portugal looked to the sea. In the 1400s, with Prince Henry the Navigator as patron, its ships worked down the coast of Africa.

  • Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488.
  • Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498.
  • Pedro Álvares Cabral reached Brazil in 1500, the start of Portuguese Brazil.
  • Forts and trading posts followed in Goa, Malacca, Macau and along the African coast.

Portuguese pepper flowed to Europe through Antwerp, and Portugal was a large carrier in the Atlantic slave trade. From 1580 to 1640 it shared a king with Spain. In 1755 the Lisbon earthquake destroyed the capital.

Brazil became independent in 1822. The monarchy fell in 1910, and a long dictatorship under Salazar followed from the 1930s. The Carnation Revolution of 1974 brought democracy and the end of colonial wars in Africa. Portugal joined the European Community in 1986.
